Use this space to write a personalized introduction to your future employer.
Your cover letter should tell a short story — one that connects who you are with the opportunity you’re pursuing. Keep your tone confident, friendly, and authentic.

Start with a strong opening that explains why you’re excited about this position and what makes you a great fit. Be genuine — share a bit about your motivation, your professional values, or a defining moment in your career that shaped your work style.

In the next paragraph, describe what you’ve accomplished in your field. Focus on the results you’ve achieved and how your contributions made a difference. Use specific examples, but keep it conversational rather than technical.
Then, explain what draws you to [Company Name] — perhaps their mission, culture, or approach to innovation. Show that you’ve done your research and that you see yourself thriving there.
Finally, close with a forward-looking statement. Express your enthusiasm to discuss the role further and invite them to contact you.
Thank the reader for their time and consideration, expressing enthusiasm to discuss the opportunity further.

Summarize your key responsibilities in 2–3 impactful sentences.

Use strong action verbs like led, improved, developed, or implemented.
Focus on outcomes rather than daily duties.

cover: Begin your letter with a strong and confident opening statement. Introduce yourself and mention the specific position title and company name to show you’ve tailored the letter. Briefly highlight what makes you a great fit — for example, your leadership experience, ability to manage complex projects, or commitment to achieving results.

In the next paragraph, connect your background to the company’s goals. Explain why you’re drawn to this organization — such as its reputation for innovation, growth, or positive impact in its industry. Demonstrate how your experience directly supports their mission by sharing one or two measurable accomplishments (e.g., increasing efficiency, reducing costs, driving performance).
Close your letter with a professional and forward-looking tone. Reaffirm your enthusiasm and invite further discussion. For instance:
“I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my skills and experience align with your company’s objectives. Please feel free to contact me at (555) 555-5555 or youremail@mail.com.”

Use this space to create a clear and polished introduction for your cover letter. Begin by briefly stating the position you’re applying for, how you learned about the opportunity, and why the role genuinely interests you. Keep the tone confident, concise, and focused on the value you aim to bring throughout your message.

In the main section of your letter, highlight the experiences, strengths, and achievements that best align with the role. Choose examples that demonstrate your capabilities and reflect the type of contribution you’re prepared to make. You can reference recent accomplishments, key skills, or moments where your work created measurable impact.
To help guide your content, consider touching on points such as:
A professional achievement that shows your ability to deliver strong results
A skill or strength that aligns directly with the role you’re seeking
A brief example of how you’ve contributed to team success or improved daily operations

Close your letter by reinforcing your interest in the position and expressing appreciation for the reader’s time and consideration. Mention that you welcome the opportunity to discuss how your background aligns with the needs of the organization.

Use this section to highlight your most impressive achievements with specific numbers or measurable results. Focus on how your skills and experience created real value for previous projects or teams. Avoid writing about what you want—instead, show employers exactly how you can help their company succeed.

<w:tab w:val="right" w:pos="10466"/></w:tabs><w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="276" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>ENTER YOUR JOB TITLE HERE</w:r><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>Date – Present
Clearly state your position title, company name, location, and dates of employment. This establishes context and credibility right away.
If you’ve earned a promotion, switched departments, or taken on higher responsibilities, make sure that progression is visible. It demonstrates growth and reliability.
In the introductory paragraph, summarize your position — mention the scope of your role, the size of the team or budget you handled, and the main focus of your work.
For less-known companies, add one concise line describing their business area or industry (e.g., “A regional logistics firm specializing in e-commerce distribution”).
Emphasize early what measurable value you added — perhaps you increased revenue, streamlined processes, launched new initiatives, or improved customer satisfaction.

<w:tab w:val="right" w:pos="10466"/></w:tabs><w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="276" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>ENTER YOUR JOB TITLE HERE</w:r><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>Date – Date

Use active, impactful verbs such as led, developed, optimized, coordinated, executed, enhanced, or innovated. These words convey ownership and initiative, unlike passive phrases such as “responsible for.”
Focus each bullet point on outcomes and contributions — not on job duties. Instead of listing what you were expected to do, describe what you actually achieved and how it benefited the organization.
Whenever possible, quantify your success. Numbers instantly add credibility — “increased client retention by 22%,” “reduced expenses by $45K annually,” or “managed a $2M annual budget.”
Prioritize your bullet points strategically: place the most impressive and job-relevant accomplishments first so they immediately capture the reader’s attention.

<w:tab w:val="right" w:pos="10466"/></w:tabs><w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="276" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>ENTER YOUR JOB TITLE HERE</w:r><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>Date – Date
Carefully review the job description and highlight repeated keywords, technical skills, and qualifications. These are what the Applicant Tracking System (ATS) is programmed to identify.
Integrate keywords naturally for balance between readability and optimization.
Remember, about 70–80% of resumes get filtered out by ATS systems simply because they lack the right phrasing. Tailoring your content for each job application increases your chances dramatically.
Use a simple and ATS-friendly format — consistent font, clear headings, and no complex graphics. When in doubt, submit your résumé as both a clean Word file and a PDF version to ensure compatibility.

<w:tab w:val="right" w:pos="10466"/></w:tabs><w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="276" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>ENTER YOUR JOB TITLE HERE</w:r><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>Date – Date
Include at least three bullet points for each position — too few might signal that your role wasn’t substantial, even if it was. If you have more to say, use concise and impactful phrasing.
Use present tense for your current job (“Manage,” “Coordinate,” “Design”) and past tense for previous roles (“Managed,” “Coordinated,” “Designed”). This subtle consistency improves readability.
Always write in an implied first-person voice. For example: “Led a cross-functional team of 10,” not “Was responsible for leading.” It sounds confident and direct.

If you took on additional responsibilities outside your formal job description — such as mentoring new hires, assisting with strategic planning, or leading a special project — include them. These details highlight initiative and leadership.

<w:tab w:val="right" w:pos="10466"/></w:tabs><w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="276" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>ENTER YOUR JOB TITLE HERE</w:r><w:r><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Inter 18pt" w:hAnsi="Inter 18pt" w:cs="Poppins"/><w:b/><w:bCs/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr><w:t>Date – Date
Proofread thoroughly before sending. Even one typo or inconsistent spacing can undermine an otherwise outstanding resume. Use tools like Grammarly or ask a trusted professional to review it.
Maintain professionalism across details — use a clean layout, a professional email address, and consistent formatting on every page. Small visual details communicate reliability.
Do a final “10-second scan” test: glance at your resume quickly and see what stands out first. Your most relevant accomplishments, metrics, and keywords should instantly catch the reader’s eye.

To ensure your resume stands out to recruiters and hiring managers, focus on communicating your professional story with authenticity and impact. Your goal is to make your background relevant and memorable.
Begin each resume section with a strong, action-focused headline that highlights your accomplishments.
Emphasize distinctive career experiences, specialized projects, or unique accomplishments that set you apart from other applicants.
Incorporate well-crafted, concise summaries that effectively communicate your professional goals, values, and career trajectory.
Provide context for your achievements to showcase depth and range.
Include relevant certifications or training to demonstrate ongoing professional development.

Show prospective employers you’re invested in both your work and the workplace. Your ability to collaborate, adapt, and contribute to company culture matters.
Mention teamwork and collaboration on successful projects.
Highlight your adaptability and eagerness to learn new technologies or processes, demonstrating your readiness to embrace change and grow with evolving business needs.

Include concise references to your leadership experiences, mentoring activities, and cross-functional contributions to showcase your ability to inspire others and collaborate effectively across teams.

Demonstrate professionalism by ensuring your resume communicates clearly and looks polished. Presentation can influence perception as much as content.
Maintain a clean, consistent formatting style with clear headings and organized sections to ensure your resume is visually appealing and easy for employers to read.
Review your resume thoroughly to identify and correct any spelling, grammar, or punctuation errors, ensuring your document is polished and professional.
Carefully avoid excessive jargon in your resume, instead choosing clear and accessible language that is specifically tailored to resonate with the requirements of the role and the industry.
Use white space and clear headings to organize your resume and make key information easy to find.

Start with a strong opening that explains why you’re excited about this position and what makes you a great fit. Be genuine — share a bit about your motivation, your professional values, or a defining moment in your career that shaped your work style.

In the next paragraph, describe what you’ve accomplished in your field. Focus on the results you’ve achieved and how your contributions made a difference. Use specific examples, but keep it conversational rather than technical.
Then, explain what draws you to [Company Name] — perhaps their mission, culture, or approach to innovation. Show that you’ve done your research and that you see yourself thriving there.
Finally, close with a forward-looking statement. Express your enthusiasm to discuss the role further and invite them to contact you.

Dear Hiring Manager (or Dear Mr. Robertson):

As a dedicated and compassionate Registered Nurse with 6+ years of experience delivering acute patient care across both high-volume hospital units and outpatient settings, I am eager to join your healthcare team and contribute to your standards of clinical excellence. I bring a patient-first philosophy combined with strong clinical judgment, thriving both in fast-paced multidisciplinary teams and in self-directed care environments.
Led and mentored 8 newly licensed nurses, guiding clinical skill development, unit orientation, and adherence to safety protocols.
Won unit "Nurse of the Quarter" award twice for clinical leadership, composure under pressure, and excellence in bedside care.
Spearheaded the overhaul of shift handoff and charting documentation, reducing preventable clinical errors by 15%.
Consistently recognized by patients, families, and supervisors for empathetic communication, achieving patient satisfaction ratings above 94%.

I bring to your organization solid clinical expertise, a proactive approach to patient safety, and a proven track record of compassionate care. I eagerly anticipate the opportunity to discuss the Registered Nurse position and explore how my experience aligns with the high-quality care your team delivers. Thank you for your time and consideration.
